# Configuration

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-config-docs.mjs from schemas/config.schema.json.
     Do not edit by hand: change the schema and run `pnpm gen:docs`. -->

Every option is optional. Without a config, the defaults below apply.

## Where the config lives

Put the config in `pw-perf.config.ts` next to `playwright.config.ts` (`.mts`, `.js`, `.mjs`,
`.cjs` and `.json` work too) and pass it to `withPerf()`:

```ts
// pw-perf.config.ts
import { definePerfConfig, perfDefaults } from 'playwright-performance-regression';

export default definePerfConfig({
  keys: { origins: { 'https://api.example.com': 'api' } },
  measure: { exclude: [...perfDefaults.measure.exclude, 'intercom.io'] },
});
```

```ts
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
import { withPerf } from 'playwright-performance-regression/config';
import perfConfig from './pw-perf.config';

export default withPerf(defineConfig({/* your config */}), perfConfig);
```

- `definePerfConfig()` returns its argument unchanged; it only adds type checking. Passing the
  object inline as the second argument of `withPerf()` works the same way.
- In a CommonJS `playwright.config.js`, a TypeScript config file loaded with `require()` arrives
  as `.default`: `withPerf(config, require('./pw-perf.config').default)`.
- A JSON config can point to the schema for editor completion:
  `"$schema": "./node_modules/playwright-performance-regression/schemas/config.schema.json"`.
- Objects are merged with the defaults; an array you set replaces the default array. To extend a
  default list, spread `perfDefaults` as in the example above.
- URL patterns may be `RegExp` objects and `keys.keyBuilder` may be a function only in a
  TypeScript or JavaScript config; a JSON config uses `{ "regex": "...", "flags": "..." }`.
- `PW_PERF_ENV` overrides `run.env`, and `PW_PERF_PASSES` overrides `run.passes.test` or
  `run.passes.thresholds` for the current mode (see [Running](cli.md)).
- An invalid config stops the run before any test with a list of all problems; see
  [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

## `$schema`

Optional, for editor support in a JSON config file: `"./node_modules/playwright-performance-regression/schemas/config.schema.json"`.

- Type: string
- Default: none

## `run`

How the measurement run is executed.

Options: [`env`](#runenv), [`passes`](#runpasses), [`grep`](#rungrep), [`keepReporters`](#runkeepreporters), [`overrideSlowMo`](#runoverrideslowmo).

### `run.env`

Environment label. Overridden by PW_PERF_ENV. Null: no label, one set of thresholds files.

- Type: string (matching `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, at most 32 characters) or `null`
- Default: `null`

### `run.passes`

Passes of the test command: the command runs once per pass and every test runs once in each pass. Overridden by PW_PERF_PASSES for the current mode.

Options: [`test`](#runpassestest), [`thresholds`](#runpassesthresholds).

### `run.passes.test`

Passes in a measurement run.

- Type: integer (1 to 1000)
- Default: `5`

### `run.passes.thresholds`

Passes in a thresholds derivation run.

- Type: integer (1 to 1000)
- Default: `10`

### `run.grep`

Only tests whose title or tags match this regular expression run in perf mode, e.g. '@perf'. Applied case-insensitively to the projects that are measured (all but setup and teardown projects); setup and teardown projects run in full. null: all tests.

- Type: `null` or string (at least 1 character)
- Default: `null`

### `run.keepReporters`

Reporters kept in perf mode by name, as in the Playwright reporter config (e.g. 'junit', 'allure-playwright'). By default withPerf() keeps only the console reporters line, dot and github (list becomes dot; name list here to keep it) and the package reporter.

- Type: array of string (at least 1 character); no duplicates
- Default: `[]`

### `run.overrideSlowMo`

Sets use.launchOptions.slowMo to 0 in every measured project in perf mode. slowMo delays every browser action and distorts the measured times; off by default because some tests are unstable without it. false: slowMo stays and perf mode warns about it (CONFIG_SLOW_MO).

- Type: boolean
- Default: `false`

## `measure`

What the collector measures.

Options: [`api`](#measureapi), [`resourceTypes`](#measureresourcetypes), [`ignoreExtensions`](#measureignoreextensions), [`include`](#measureinclude), [`exclude`](#measureexclude), [`excludeKnownThirdParty`](#measureexcludeknownthirdparty), [`successStatuses`](#measuresuccessstatuses), [`steps`](#measuresteps), [`pendingTimeoutMs`](#measurependingtimeoutms).

### `measure.api`

Requests the browser makes to the backend and calls of the request fixture, page.request and context.request (keys with the prefix 'request '), as keys of kind 'api'. false: no request is measured, the api thresholds file is neither read nor written, and only test.step durations are measured; measure.api and measure.steps cannot both be off.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `measure.resourceTypes`

Playwright resource types that are measured. WebSocket traffic is not available as Request events in Playwright and cannot be measured.

- Type: array of one of `"document"`, `"stylesheet"`, `"image"`, `"media"`, `"font"`, `"script"`, `"texttrack"`, `"xhr"`, `"fetch"`, `"eventsource"`, `"manifest"`, `"other"`; at least 1 item, no duplicates
- Default: `["document","xhr","fetch"]`

### `measure.ignoreExtensions`

Requests whose URL path ends with one of these extensions are skipped, except resource type 'document'.

- Type: array of string (matching `^\.[a-z0-9]+$`); no duplicates
- Default: `[".js",".mjs",".css",".map",".html",".png",".jpg",".jpeg",".gif",".svg",".webp",".avif",".ico",".woff",".woff2",".ttf",".otf",".eot"]`

### `measure.include`

When not empty, only requests whose URL matches at least one pattern are measured.

- Type: array of [URL pattern](#url-patterns)
- Default: `[]`

### `measure.exclude`

Requests whose URL matches any pattern are skipped. Applied after include.

- Type: array of [URL pattern](#url-patterns)
- Default: `["/socket.io/"]`

### `measure.excludeKnownThirdParty`

Skip requests to the built-in list of analytics, tag manager, monitoring and chat hosts.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `measure.successStatuses`

HTTP statuses counted as successful samples: a class like '2xx' or an exact code like '404'.

- Type: array of string (matching `^(?:[1-5]xx|[1-5][0-9]{2})$`); at least 1 item, no duplicates
- Default: `["2xx","3xx"]`

### `measure.steps`

Durations of test.step steps as keys of kind 'step'. true (default) enables with defaults, false disables, an object enables with settings.

- Type: boolean or object
- Default: `true`

### `measure.pendingTimeoutMs`

How long the collector waits at test end for requests still in flight.

- Type: integer (0 to 60000)
- Default: `2000`

## `keys`

How raw URLs become endpoint keys.

Options: [`origins`](#keysorigins), [`idPatterns`](#keysidpatterns), [`extraIdPatterns`](#keysextraidpatterns), [`query`](#keysquery), [`keepQueryValues`](#keyskeepqueryvalues), [`dropQueryParams`](#keysdropqueryparams), [`keyBuilder`](#keyskeybuilder).

### `keys.origins`

Origin to label mapping, e.g. {"https://api.example.com": "api"}. A key with `*` is a host pattern, e.g. `"https://*.ci.example.com"` (one `*` per host label, never across a dot); an exact entry wins over a pattern. The origin of Playwright use.baseURL gets the empty label unless mapped here. Other origins are labeled with their host.

- Type: object with keys matching `^(?:https?://[^/?#]+|.*\*.*)$` and values of type string (matching `^[a-z0-9.-]*$`, at most 64 characters)
- Default: `{}`

### `keys.idPatterns`

Built-in path segment patterns replaced with ':id'.

Options: [`number`](#keysidpatternsnumber), [`uuid`](#keysidpatternsuuid), [`hex`](#keysidpatternshex), [`token`](#keysidpatternstoken), [`mixed`](#keysidpatternsmixed), [`prefixed`](#keysidpatternsprefixed), [`email`](#keysidpatternsemail).

### `keys.idPatterns.number`

Path segments made only of digits.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `keys.idPatterns.uuid`

UUIDs in any letter case.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `keys.idPatterns.hex`

Hex strings of at least 16 characters.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `keys.idPatterns.token`

Tokens of at least 24 characters containing a digit, without separators or with mixed case.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `keys.idPatterns.mixed`

Random-looking ids of at least 16 characters with a digit, a lowercase and an uppercase letter, e.g. nanoid.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `keys.idPatterns.prefixed`

Ids with a prefix: 2-5 capital letters, '-' and at least 3 digits (ORD-1000), or 1-8 lowercase letters, '_' and at least 2 digits or 8-32 letters and digits with a digit (inv_58).

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `keys.idPatterns.email`

E-mail addresses, replaced with ':email'.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `keys.extraIdPatterns`

Additional path segment patterns replaced with ':id'. A string matches a whole segment literally; a regex is tested against the segment.

- Type: array of [URL pattern](#url-patterns)
- Default: `[]`

### `keys.query`

'names': keep sorted parameter names; 'ignore': drop the query string entirely.

- Type: one of `"names"`, `"ignore"`
- Default: `"names"`

### `keys.keepQueryValues`

Query parameters whose values are kept in the key, e.g. ['type'] gives '?type=open'.

- Type: array of string (at least 1 character); no duplicates
- Default: `[]`

### `keys.dropQueryParams`

Query parameter names always removed from the key (e.g. cache busters with fixed names).

- Type: array of string (at least 1 character); no duplicates
- Default: `[]`

### `keys.keyBuilder`

Builds the endpoint key of a request yourself. Return a string to use it as the key, or `undefined` to fall back to the built-in rules. For calls of the `request` fixture, `page.request` and `context.request` it gets `resourceType: "request"`, and the key gets the prefix `request ` after it. Not allowed in a JSON config file; the run report records it as `"[function]"`.

- Type: function `({ method, url, resourceType }) => string | undefined` (TypeScript or JavaScript config only)
- Default: none

## `checks`

What is checked for every key and how thresholds are derived for it. Each rule: enabled, minSamples, limit (for keys without an entry in the thresholds file) and margin (headroom added when deriving thresholds).

Options: [`time`](#checkstime), [`slowShare`](#checksslowshare), [`errors`](#checkserrors).

### `checks.time`

Response-time rules.

Options: [`median`](#checkstimemedian), [`percentile`](#checkstimepercentile), [`p99`](#checkstimep99).

### `checks.time.median`

Median (p50) must not exceed the limit.

Options: [`enabled`](#checkstimemedianenabled), [`minSamples`](#checkstimemedianminsamples), [`margin`](#checkstimemedianmargin), [`limit`](#checkstimemedianlimit).

### `checks.time.median.enabled`

Run this rule.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `checks.time.median.minSamples`

Minimum samples for the rule to run.

- Type: integer (at least 1)
- Default: `5`

### `checks.time.median.margin`

Headroom added to the source run value when deriving this limit.

Options: [`relative`](#checkstimemedianmarginrelative), [`minMs`](#checkstimemedianmarginminms), [`smallSampleRelative`](#checkstimemedianmarginsmallsamplerelative).

### `checks.time.median.margin.relative`

Relative headroom, e.g. 0.4 = +40%.

- Type: number (0 to 10)
- Default: `0.4`

### `checks.time.median.margin.minMs`

Minimum absolute headroom in ms.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: `100`

### `checks.time.median.margin.smallSampleRelative`

Relative headroom when the key has fewer than thresholds.smallSampleN samples.

- Type: number (0 to 10)
- Default: `0.8`

### `checks.time.median.limit`

Limit in ms for keys without an entry in the thresholds file.

Options: [`api`](#checkstimemedianlimitapi), [`step`](#checkstimemedianlimitstep).

### `checks.time.median.limit.api`

Threshold limit in whole milliseconds, rounded up.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: `2000`

### `checks.time.median.limit.step`

Threshold limit in whole milliseconds, rounded up.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: `10000`

### `checks.time.percentile`

The percentile chosen in level must not exceed the limit.

Options: [`enabled`](#checkstimepercentileenabled), [`minSamples`](#checkstimepercentileminsamples), [`level`](#checkstimepercentilelevel), [`limit`](#checkstimepercentilelimit), [`margin`](#checkstimepercentilemargin).

### `checks.time.percentile.enabled`

Run this rule.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `checks.time.percentile.minSamples`

Minimum samples for the rule to run.

- Type: integer (at least 1)
- Default: `20`

### `checks.time.percentile.level`

Which percentile this rule evaluates, e.g. p95 (the thresholds file records it as evaluatedPercentile).

- Type: string (matching `^p(?:[1-9][0-9]?)(?:\.[0-9])?$`)
- Default: `"p95"`

### `checks.time.percentile.limit`

Limit in ms for keys without an entry in the thresholds file.

Options: [`api`](#checkstimepercentilelimitapi), [`step`](#checkstimepercentilelimitstep).

### `checks.time.percentile.limit.api`

Threshold limit in whole milliseconds, rounded up.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: `2000`

### `checks.time.percentile.limit.step`

Threshold limit in whole milliseconds, rounded up.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: `15000`

### `checks.time.percentile.margin`

Headroom added to the source run value when deriving this limit.

Options: [`relative`](#checkstimepercentilemarginrelative), [`minMs`](#checkstimepercentilemarginminms), [`smallSampleRelative`](#checkstimepercentilemarginsmallsamplerelative).

### `checks.time.percentile.margin.relative`

Relative headroom, e.g. 0.4 = +40%.

- Type: number (0 to 10)
- Default: `0.4`

### `checks.time.percentile.margin.minMs`

Minimum absolute headroom in ms.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: `100`

### `checks.time.percentile.margin.smallSampleRelative`

Relative headroom when the key has fewer than thresholds.smallSampleN samples.

- Type: number (0 to 10)
- Default: `0.8`

### `checks.time.p99`

p99 must not exceed the limit.

Options: [`enabled`](#checkstimep99enabled), [`minSamples`](#checkstimep99minsamples), [`margin`](#checkstimep99margin), [`limit`](#checkstimep99limit).

### `checks.time.p99.enabled`

Run this rule.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `checks.time.p99.minSamples`

Minimum samples for the rule to run.

- Type: integer (at least 1)
- Default: `100`

### `checks.time.p99.margin`

Headroom added to the source run value when deriving this limit.

Options: [`relative`](#checkstimep99marginrelative), [`minGapMs`](#checkstimep99marginmingapms), [`minGapRelative`](#checkstimep99marginmingaprelative).

### `checks.time.p99.margin.relative`

Relative headroom over the source p99.

- Type: number (0 to 10)
- Default: `0.2`

### `checks.time.p99.margin.minGapMs`

The p99 limit is at least this many ms above the percentile limit.

- Type: integer (at least 1)
- Default: `50`

### `checks.time.p99.margin.minGapRelative`

The p99 limit is at least this share above the percentile limit.

- Type: number (0 to 10)
- Default: `0.1`

### `checks.time.p99.limit`

Limit in ms for keys without an entry in the thresholds file.

Options: [`api`](#checkstimep99limitapi), [`step`](#checkstimep99limitstep).

### `checks.time.p99.limit.api`

Threshold limit in whole milliseconds, rounded up.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: `4000`

### `checks.time.p99.limit.step`

Threshold limit in whole milliseconds, rounded up.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: `30000`

### `checks.slowShare`

Rules on the share of slow responses, relative to the Apdex threshold T. Run only for keys with a key-specific T from the thresholds file.

Options: [`t`](#checksslowsharet), [`apdex`](#checksslowshareapdex), [`wilson`](#checksslowsharewilson).

### `checks.slowShare.t`

Apdex threshold T: satisfied below T, tolerated up to 4T. Used by the apdex and wilson rules, which run only for keys whose thresholds file entry has a key-specific t. These settings bound the derived T.

Options: [`api`](#checksslowsharetapi), [`step`](#checksslowsharetstep).

### `checks.slowShare.t.api`

Options: [`min`](#checksslowsharetapimin), [`max`](#checksslowsharetapimax), [`medianFactor`](#checksslowsharetapimedianfactor).

### `checks.slowShare.t.api.min`

Lower clamp of derived T.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: none

### `checks.slowShare.t.api.max`

Upper clamp of derived T; when p50 is above it, t, minApdex and maxWilson are null.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: none

### `checks.slowShare.t.api.medianFactor`

Derived T is at most medianFactor × p50.

- Type: number (1 to 10)
- Default: none

### `checks.slowShare.t.step`

Options: [`min`](#checksslowsharetstepmin), [`max`](#checksslowsharetstepmax), [`medianFactor`](#checksslowsharetstepmedianfactor).

### `checks.slowShare.t.step.min`

Lower clamp of derived T.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: none

### `checks.slowShare.t.step.max`

Upper clamp of derived T; when p50 is above it, t, minApdex and maxWilson are null.

- Type: integer (at least 0)
- Default: none

### `checks.slowShare.t.step.medianFactor`

Derived T is at most medianFactor × p50.

- Type: number (1 to 10)
- Default: none

### `checks.slowShare.apdex`

Apdex(T) must not fall below the limit (upper confidence bound compared). Runs only for keys with a key-specific T from the thresholds file.

Options: [`enabled`](#checksslowshareapdexenabled), [`minSamples`](#checksslowshareapdexminsamples), [`margin`](#checksslowshareapdexmargin), [`limit`](#checksslowshareapdexlimit).

### `checks.slowShare.apdex.enabled`

Run this rule.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `checks.slowShare.apdex.minSamples`

Minimum samples for the rule to run.

- Type: integer (at least 1)
- Default: `20`

### `checks.slowShare.apdex.margin`

Headroom added to the source run value when deriving this limit.

Options: [`absolute`](#checksslowshareapdexmarginabsolute), [`smallSampleAbsolute`](#checksslowshareapdexmarginsmallsampleabsolute).

### `checks.slowShare.apdex.margin.absolute`

Subtracted from the source Apdex.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.05`

### `checks.slowShare.apdex.margin.smallSampleAbsolute`

Subtracted when the key has fewer than thresholds.smallSampleN samples.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.1`

### `checks.slowShare.apdex.limit`

minApdex for hand-written thresholds file entries that set t but omit minApdex. Keys without an entry never run this rule.

Options: [`api`](#checksslowshareapdexlimitapi), [`step`](#checksslowshareapdexlimitstep).

### `checks.slowShare.apdex.limit.api`

Value between 0 and 1 inclusive. The thresholds generator writes at most 3 decimal places; hand-written values with more decimals are accepted.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.85`

### `checks.slowShare.apdex.limit.step`

Value between 0 and 1 inclusive. The thresholds generator writes at most 3 decimal places; hand-written values with more decimals are accepted.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.85`

### `checks.slowShare.wilson`

Share of samples slower than T must not exceed the limit (lower Wilson bound compared). Runs only for keys with a key-specific T.

Options: [`enabled`](#checksslowsharewilsonenabled), [`minSamples`](#checksslowsharewilsonminsamples), [`margin`](#checksslowsharewilsonmargin), [`limit`](#checksslowsharewilsonlimit).

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.enabled`

Run this rule.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.minSamples`

Minimum samples for the rule to run.

- Type: integer (at least 1)
- Default: `20`

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.margin`

Headroom added to the source run value when deriving this limit.

Options: [`factor`](#checksslowsharewilsonmarginfactor), [`add`](#checksslowsharewilsonmarginadd), [`min`](#checksslowsharewilsonmarginmin), [`max`](#checksslowsharewilsonmarginmax), [`smallSampleMin`](#checksslowsharewilsonmarginsmallsamplemin).

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.margin.factor`

Multiplier of the source share of slow samples.

- Type: number (0 to 10)
- Default: `1.5`

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.margin.add`

Added after multiplying.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.02`

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.margin.min`

Lower clamp of the derived limit.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.03`

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.margin.max`

Upper clamp of the derived limit (self-consistency may exceed it).

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.15`

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.margin.smallSampleMin`

Minimum limit when the key has fewer than thresholds.smallSampleN samples.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.1`

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.limit`

maxWilson for hand-written thresholds file entries that set t but omit maxWilson. Keys without an entry never run this rule.

Options: [`api`](#checksslowsharewilsonlimitapi), [`step`](#checksslowsharewilsonlimitstep).

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.limit.api`

Value between 0 and 1 inclusive. The thresholds generator writes at most 3 decimal places; hand-written values with more decimals are accepted.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.05`

### `checks.slowShare.wilson.limit.step`

Value between 0 and 1 inclusive. The thresholds generator writes at most 3 decimal places; hand-written values with more decimals are accepted.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.05`

### `checks.errors`

Error rate must not exceed the limit (lower Wilson bound compared).

Options: [`enabled`](#checkserrorsenabled), [`minSamples`](#checkserrorsminsamples), [`statuses`](#checkserrorsstatuses), [`limit`](#checkserrorslimit), [`margin`](#checkserrorsmargin).

### `checks.errors.enabled`

Run this rule.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `checks.errors.minSamples`

Minimum samples for the rule to run.

- Type: integer (at least 1)
- Default: `5`

### `checks.errors.statuses`

Request statuses counted as errors by the 'errors' rule: a class like '5xx', an exact code like '429', FAILED (request failed without a response, not aborted), ABORTED (cancelled by the browser, e.g. on navigation), PENDING (still in flight at test end).

- Type: array of string (matching `^(?:[1-5]xx|[1-5][0-9]{2}|FAILED|ABORTED|PENDING)$`); no duplicates
- Default: `["5xx","FAILED","PENDING"]`

### `checks.errors.limit`

Limit for keys without an entry in the thresholds file.

Options: [`api`](#checkserrorslimitapi), [`step`](#checkserrorslimitstep).

### `checks.errors.limit.api`

Value between 0 and 1 inclusive. The thresholds generator writes at most 3 decimal places; hand-written values with more decimals are accepted.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.05`

### `checks.errors.limit.step`

Value between 0 and 1 inclusive. The thresholds generator writes at most 3 decimal places; hand-written values with more decimals are accepted.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.05`

### `checks.errors.margin`

Headroom added to the source run value when deriving this limit.

Options: [`factor`](#checkserrorsmarginfactor), [`add`](#checkserrorsmarginadd), [`min`](#checkserrorsmarginmin).

### `checks.errors.margin.factor`

Multiplier of the source error rate.

- Type: number (0 to 10)
- Default: `1.5`

### `checks.errors.margin.add`

Added after multiplying.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.02`

### `checks.errors.margin.min`

Minimum derived limit.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.05`

## `gate`

Gate policy: when violations fail the run.

Options: [`tolerance`](#gatetolerance), [`hardLimitFactor`](#gatehardlimitfactor), [`defaultThresholds`](#gatedefaultthresholds), [`maxFailedTestShare`](#gatemaxfailedtestshare).

### `gate.tolerance`

Number of keys with violations that is still tolerated: an integer, or a percentage of evaluated keys like '5%'. 0: every violation blocks.

- Type: integer (at least 0) or string (matching `^(?:100|[0-9]{1,2}(?:\.[0-9]+)?)%$`)
- Default: `0`

### `gate.hardLimitFactor`

A time check exceeding limit x factor always blocks, regardless of tolerance. Null disables hard limits.

- Type: number (at least 1) or `null`
- Default: `2`

### `gate.defaultThresholds`

'block': violations on keys evaluated with default thresholds can fail the run; 'warn': they only warn.

- Type: one of `"block"`, `"warn"`
- Default: `"block"`

### `gate.maxFailedTestShare`

Highest share of failed test executions (unexpected / executed, skipped excluded) for which the run result is still trustworthy. Above it the run ends with tool error TESTS_FAILED_TOO_MANY (exit code 3). Failed tests below it are a warning only: in perf mode the performance result decides.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.1`

## `thresholds`

Thresholds files and derivation.

Options: [`preset`](#thresholdspreset), [`dir`](#thresholdsdir), [`filePrefix`](#thresholdsfileprefix), [`update`](#thresholdsupdate), [`smallSampleN`](#thresholdssmallsamplen), [`hysteresis`](#thresholdshysteresis), [`loosenWarnRelative`](#thresholdsloosenwarnrelative).

### `thresholds.preset`

Headroom preset for derived thresholds: sets the defaults of every `checks.*.margin`; margin fields set explicitly win. strict: small headroom, catches smaller regressions, more false alarms on a noisy environment. normal: recommended start. loose: large headroom, only clear regressions, for shared noisy environments.

- Type: one of `"strict"`, `"normal"`, `"loose"`
- Default: `"normal"`

### `thresholds.dir`

Directory of thresholds files, relative to the Playwright config directory.

- Type: string (at least 1 character)
- Default: `"."`

### `thresholds.filePrefix`

File name prefix; files are `<prefix>[.steps][.<env>].json`.

- Type: string (matching `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`)
- Default: `"pw-perf-thresholds"`

### `thresholds.update`

'all': recompute every unlocked complete entry (with hysteresis); 'new-only': add entries for new keys, keep existing ones.

- Type: one of `"all"`, `"new-only"`
- Default: `"all"`

### `thresholds.smallSampleN`

Keys with fewer samples get the small-sample headroom (`checks.*.margin.smallSample*`) when deriving thresholds.

- Type: integer (at least 1)
- Default: `20`

### `thresholds.hysteresis`

When re-deriving, an existing unlocked entry keeps its limit if the new value differs by less than this. Avoids noise-only diffs.

Options: [`relative`](#thresholdshysteresisrelative), [`ratio`](#thresholdshysteresisratio).

### `thresholds.hysteresis.relative`

For ms limits: relative difference, e.g. 0.1 = 10%.

- Type: number (0 to 1)
- Default: `0.1`

### `thresholds.hysteresis.ratio`

For ratio limits: absolute difference. At most 0.01 so a kept entry stays self-consistent.

- Type: number (0 to 0.01)
- Default: `0.01`

### `thresholds.loosenWarnRelative`

Warn (THRESHOLDS_LOOSENED_MUCH) when a derived time limit grows by more than this share.

- Type: number (0 to 100)
- Default: `0.5`

## `report`

Run outputs.

Options: [`dir`](#reportdir), [`html`](#reporthtml), [`rawUrls`](#reportrawurls).

### `report.dir`

Directory of report.json and report.html, relative to the Playwright config directory. Emptied when the first test of a test or thresholds run starts; never the project directory or a folder with thresholds files.

- Type: string (at least 1 character)
- Default: `"reports/pw-perf"`

### `report.html`

Write the HTML report.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `true`

### `report.rawUrls`

Include raw URLs of the slowest samples in the run report.

- Type: boolean
- Default: `false`

## `advanced`

Rarely changed settings.

Options: [`maxSamplesPerKey`](#advancedmaxsamplesperkey), [`seed`](#advancedseed).

### `advanced.maxSamplesPerKey`

Successful durations retained per key.

- Type: integer (100 to 100000)
- Default: `5000`

### `advanced.seed`

Seed of the sampling random generator.

- Type: integer (0 to 4294967295)
- Default: `1`

## URL patterns

`measure.include`, `measure.exclude` and `keys.extraIdPatterns` take a list of patterns:

- a string matches as a case-sensitive substring of the full URL (for `keys.extraIdPatterns`:
  a whole path segment, literally);
- `{ "regex": "...", "flags": "..." }` is a JavaScript regular expression;
- in a TypeScript or JavaScript config, a `RegExp` works as well.

The `g` and `y` flags are ignored, so a pattern matches the same way on every call.

Example: ids that the built-in `keys.idPatterns` miss, such as `ord.1000`, `2026-Q4-17` or the
fixed id `demo-tenant`, split one endpoint into many keys (the run warns with
`NORMALIZE_HIGH_CARDINALITY`). Each pattern is tested against one whole path segment:

```ts
keys: {
  extraIdPatterns: [
    /^ord\.[0-9]+$/, // GET /orders/ord.1000 → GET /orders/:id
    /^[0-9]{4}-Q[1-4]-[0-9]+$/, // GET /reports/2026-Q4-17 → GET /reports/:id
    'demo-tenant', // GET /t/demo-tenant/users → GET /t/:id/users
  ],
}
```

In a JSON config: `"extraIdPatterns": [{ "regex": "^ord\\.[0-9]+$" }, "demo-tenant"]`.
